summary.figures: 3 inline SVG (bar chart, population pyramid, cyclone track map) + 1 HTML data table

families.outcome: Calculate and interpret population density, and judge claims about crowding against data
families.context: A three-district table of population and area (Port Louis, Plaines Wilhems, Savanne) in which the largest population is NOT the densest district

variants.variation: apply the definition once: divide one row's population by its area
variants.misconception: divides area by population and returns a meaningless decimal

variants.variation: compute three densities and rank them, then name the district
variants.misconception: names the district with the largest population, treating population as crowding

variants.variation: reverse it — density and area given, population withheld (real Moka figures, 360 x 230)
variants.misconception: divides because density questions usually involve division

variants.variation: judge a written pupil claim against the table and say why it fails
variants.misconception: confuses total population with density; a rival option offers largest area as crowding

variants.variation: decide what information is MISSING before a schools decision can be taken
variants.misconception: thinks a crowded district automatically needs schools; three options are already given or derivable

families.outcome: Read values and changes off a bar chart and test a prediction against them
families.context: Inline-SVG bar chart of tourist arrivals 2019-2023 (1400, 300, 200, 1000, 1300 thousand) read against a labelled 200-unit scale

variants.variation: read two bars and find the difference
variants.misconception: adds the two bars because both are used

variants.variation: compare every consecutive pair to find the largest FALL, not the lowest value
variants.misconception: answers 2021 because it is the shortest bar

variants.variation: evaluate a manager's 'risen every year' claim step by step, then his forecast
variants.misconception: reads an overall upward shape as an every-year rise; arrivals actually fell 2020 to 2021

variants.variation: convert a read change into a percentage increase (200 to 1000 = 400%)
variants.misconception: answers 500% — the new figure as a percentage of the old, not the increase

families.outcome: Distinguish import substitution from export-led industrialisation and explain why the second suited Mauritius
families.context: The zone created by the Act of 1970 and the policy it replaced

variants.variation: produce the term from a description of the policy rather than pick it
variants.misconception: writes ISI, the earlier and opposite policy

variants.variation: name the dominant industry of the zone in one word
variants.misconception: answers sugar, the sector the zone existed to reduce dependence on

variants.variation: diagnose the error in a pupil's written sentence
variants.misconception: merges the two policies because both aimed at industry; they face opposite markets

variants.variation: compare two policy options under the stated constraint of a tiny home market
variants.misconception: judges a policy by whether it sounds protective rather than by the constraint it must beat

variants.variation: calculate value added, not turnover, on a duty-free import (150 - 60) x 4000
variants.misconception: multiplies the selling price by the quantity and calls that the gain to Mauritius

families.outcome: Explain why a small economy joins regional bodies, and test duty-free access against a better price
families.context: A Mauritian garment firm choosing between a COMESA buyer and a buyer outside the agreement

variants.variation: complete the name of the organisation from its opening words
variants.misconception: answers Asia because Mauritius trades heavily with India

variants.variation: resolve an apparent contradiction — no resources, yet many memberships
variants.misconception: treats membership as a reward for size or wealth rather than a strategy for smallness

variants.variation: compute what the firm KEEPS under each offer and find the difference (Rs 12 500 the other way)
variants.misconception: assumes duty-free access always wins, so never computes the net price

variants.variation: change one condition — which change would flip the decision (Rs 460 less 15% = Rs 391)
variants.misconception: treats any change as relevant; two options make the other offer better still, one affects both equally

families.outcome: Calculate VAT forwards and backwards and judge who a flat rate falls hardest on
families.context: A shop receipt and the 15% VAT collected by the MRA

variants.variation: produce the collecting authority's abbreviation
variants.misconception: names the Ministry of Finance, which sets rates but does not collect

variants.variation: add VAT to a price given before tax
variants.misconception: takes the percentage of the wrong one of the two prices

variants.variation: argue against a fairness claim using what households earn, not what they pay
variants.misconception: judges fairness from the rate alone; the same rate is not the same burden

variants.variation: reverse it — extract the VAT already inside a total (4600 / 1.15)
variants.misconception: takes 15% of the VAT-inclusive total and answers 690

families.outcome: Classify media and separate what a source shows from what it claims
families.context: A false cyclone warning forwarded phone to phone, and two accounts of one road accident

variants.variation: name the media type from two named platforms
variants.misconception: answers print media because a post contains writing

variants.variation: identify which difference between a post and a newspaper actually matters
variants.misconception: believes reach or speed makes a message reliable, rather than editorial responsibility

variants.variation: weigh two competing accounts and separate footage from the caption on it
variants.misconception: treats a caption as part of the evidence — a literal record versus an inference

variants.variation: name the constitutional freedom behind the watchdog role
variants.misconception: answers with another protected right, such as freedom of movement

families.outcome: Classify family types by household composition and reason about family change without assuming cause
families.context: One three-generation household, and the national trends in women's work and household size

variants.variation: name the type from a described household
variants.misconception: answers nuclear; the number of generations in the household is the test

variants.variation: change one condition — the grandparents move out — and say what follows
variants.misconception: keeps calling it extended because the relatives are still nearby

variants.variation: evaluate a causal conclusion drawn from two trends moving together
variants.misconception: correlation read as one-way causation; the arrow can point the other way

variants.variation: name the function being performed in a described situation
variants.misconception: answers economic because the family is providing something

families.outcome: Explain the detachment of the Chagos Archipelago and what a court opinion can and cannot do
families.context: The 1965 detachment, the base on Diego Garcia and the 2019 ICJ advisory opinion

variants.variation: give the year, anchored three years before independence
variants.misconception: writes 1968 (independence) or 1992 (republic)

variants.variation: resolve an apparent contradiction between 1968 independence and the claim of no consent
variants.misconception: assumes an independent state must have agreed; the decision came before independence

variants.variation: judge what a 2019 advisory opinion actually changed on the ground
variants.misconception: treats a legal finding as its own enforcement; a rival option confuses Chagos with Tromelin

variants.variation: name the island carrying the base
variants.misconception: answers Tromelin, the other disputed island, which has no such base

families.outcome: Read positions and direction off a latitude-longitude grid and interpret a cyclone track
families.context: Inline-SVG track map, 54-64 E by 14-24 S, four dated centre positions and Mauritius marked

variants.variation: read latitude for a stated longitude
variants.misconception: reads the bottom scale and gives the longitude instead

variants.variation: combine two readings into a compass direction of travel
variants.misconception: answers due south after noticing only the latitude change

variants.variation: judge a claim that a near miss means no effect
variants.misconception: reads a track line as the boundary of the storm; the dots mark only the centre

variants.variation: convert degrees of latitude read off the grid into km (6 x 111)
variants.misconception: counts the dots instead of the degrees, or uses the longitude change

families.outcome: Read a population pyramid, calculate a dependency ratio from it, and test claims about the future
families.context: Inline-SVG age-sex pyramid, six bands, every bar landing on a 25-thousand tick (total 1.2 million)

variants.variation: read one bar against the scale
variants.misconception: reads the male bar on the other side of the same row

variants.variation: group six bars into the working-age band and total them
variants.misconception: includes the 0-14 band because school pupils are not working

variants.variation: choose which of four TRUE readings of the chart is evidence of ageing
variants.misconception: accepts any true statement as evidence; three describe longevity or sex balance

variants.variation: apply a supplied definition across twelve bars: 450 dependants per 750 workers
variants.misconception: counts only children as dependants and forgets the two oldest bands

variants.variation: judge a minister's forecast of school demand from the shape of the base
variants.misconception: compares the young band with the old bands instead of with the bands just above it

families.outcome: State the obstacles of the 1960s and explain why the pessimistic forecast failed
families.context: The 1961 Meade report and what changed after 1970

variants.variation: name the single export crop the forecast rested on
variants.misconception: answers tea or tobacco, both grown but neither the dependence

variants.variation: select the PAIR of conditions, not a single cause
variants.misconception: thinks smallness alone was the problem, rather than growth plus dependence

variants.variation: explain why a prediction failed by testing each of its assumptions
variants.misconception: looks for one lucky event (a sugar price, aid) instead of the assumptions changing

variants.variation: produce the one-word name of the strategy
variants.misconception: answers industrialisation, which leaves out tourism and services

families.outcome: Explain how distance shapes services in Rodrigues and Agalega and choose between two ways of providing them
families.context: Health provision and transport links for the outer islands

variants.variation: name the autonomous body created in 2002
variants.misconception: answers the National Assembly, the parliament of the whole Republic

variants.variation: apply density to a small island (44 000 over 110 km squared)
variants.misconception: assumes a small island must be crowded, without dividing

variants.variation: choose the criterion that should decide between a resident specialist and more flights
variants.misconception: picks the option that costs less in the first year instead of the one that meets the need

variants.variation: change one condition — a longer airstrip and deeper jetty — and predict what follows
variants.misconception: expects infrastructure to create institutions or industries by itself

families.outcome: Classify a move, separate push from pull, and judge an absolute claim about emigration
families.context: A nurse's move from Souillac to Curepipe, set beside national migration flows

variants.variation: classify a move in one word
variants.misconception: answers emigration, though no border has been crossed

variants.variation: sort relevant from irrelevant detail — one push, one pull, two neutral facts
variants.misconception: treats every fact in the stem as a factor, or calls the closed clinic a pull

variants.variation: decide whether an absolute claim is always, sometimes or never true
variants.misconception: answers always because the claim sounds reasonable; remittances and returning skills are the exception

variants.variation: compute net migration from two flows
variants.misconception: adds the flows and answers 9 900, the number who moved, not the net effect

notes: Every calculated answer was re-derived independently from the data as printed: 280, 82 800, 800, 400%, Rs 360 000, Rs 12 500, Rs 345, Rs 600, 1965, 18 degrees, 666 km, 100, 750, 60, 400, 1 500. Every division is exact.

No variant discloses another's answer. Three items were rewritten after a first pass did: fam-001-d named the densest district (fam-001-b's answer), fam-006-b printed 'social media' (fam-006-a's answer), and fam-008-b printed 1965 (fam-008-a's answer).
fam-010-c and fam-010-e originally rested on the same reading of the pyramid; -c now tests 60+ against under-15 (250 vs 200) and -e the narrowing base, so the two no longer answer each other.

Mauritius figures used: EPZ Act 1970 and textiles-dominated (consistent with g9sms-v034 and g9sms-pi043 already in the pack); VAT 15%; Chagos detached 1965, ICJ advisory opinion 2019, base on Diego Garcia; Rodrigues Regional Assembly 2002; Moka about 230 km squared and about 82 800 people. The district table is labelled 'figures rounded' and the arrivals chart uses figures rounded to 0.1 million, so no item depends on a figure to a precision this repo cannot support. Nothing in the batch depends on the status of the 2024-25 Chagos negotiations.

FOUND, NOT CHANGED (existing bank): g9sms-pi054 trips the 'refers to the textbook' check in test-option-parity.js. g9sms-v084 uses Port Louis 118 000 / 43 km squared while my table uses 129 000 / 43; both are labelled approximate but the pack would read better with one agreed set of district figures. And the pack carries 98 items whose correct option is materially the longest and an average option spread of 16.8 characters, which is the real reason test-option-parity.js fails for this pack - it is a backlog in the existing five files, not in this batch.
